title: Decide whether the requirement justifies a mesh
description: Select the primary networking requirement and the team that will own it. The model recommends the first approach that covers every required control and meets its minimum operating readiness.

capabilities.label: Public edge routing
capabilities.detail: Route external traffic by host, path, or header before it enters the service network.

capabilities.label: Service discovery
capabilities.detail: Resolve a stable service name to the current set of healthy workload endpoints.

capabilities.label: Request deadlines
capabilities.detail: Bound each call inside the caller's end-to-end latency budget.

capabilities.label: Retry policy
capabilities.detail: Repeat only eligible transient failures while limiting attempt amplification.

capabilities.label: Uniform network telemetry
capabilities.detail: Observe request rate, errors, and duration across services and runtimes.

capabilities.label: Workload identity
capabilities.detail: Authenticate a workload with a rotated identity instead of trusting source IP alone.

capabilities.label: East-west mutual TLS
capabilities.detail: Encrypt and mutually authenticate communication between participating internal workloads.

capabilities.label: Service authorization
capabilities.detail: Allow or deny internal calls from stable workload identities at the destination boundary.

capabilities.label: Weighted internal routing
capabilities.detail: Shift selected service-to-service traffic between versions without changing every caller.

scenarios.label: Expose one public API
scenarios.detail: External clients need host and path routing to stable Kubernetes Services.

scenarios.label: Standardize one runtime
scenarios.detail: Services in one application stack need consistent deadlines, bounded retries, and request telemetry.

scenarios.label: Protect internal service calls
scenarios.detail: Multiple teams need rotated workload identity, mutual TLS, least-privilege authorization, and network evidence.

scenarios.label: Run cross-runtime canaries
scenarios.detail: Callers in several languages need the same weighted internal routing, retry bounds, and telemetry.

readiness.label: Application teams only
readiness.detail: No team owns shared networking policy, certificates, upgrades, or mesh incidents.

readiness.label: Part-time platform owner
readiness.detail: A platform team can run a pilot, but has no dedicated mesh on-call or upgrade program.

readiness.label: Dedicated platform product
readiness.detail: Named owners support policy review, capacity, upgrades, dashboards, incidents, and rollback.

approaches.label: Kubernetes Services plus gateway
approaches.detail: Keep internal discovery in Kubernetes and apply public host or path routing at the edge.
approaches.operatingShape: Cluster networking and gateway ownership; no mesh data plane

approaches.label: Shared application libraries
approaches.detail: Put deadlines, retry rules, and telemetry in a supported runtime library owned with the applications.
approaches.operatingShape: Application release process and runtime-specific library maintenance

approaches.label: Service mesh
approaches.detail: Add a control plane and data-plane enforcement for consistent internal identity, routing, authorization, and telemetry.
approaches.operatingShape: Dedicated platform ownership for data plane, control plane, identity, policy, and upgrades
